Reference / collections/iteration

collections/iteration#

How for walks a collection: an Iterating gives a Cursor, and a Batching gives batches.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

for collection -> item { … }              // any Iterating or Batching

let cursor = collection.cursor();
if cursor.available() {
    cursor.item();
    cursor.successor();
}

Description#

How for walks a collection: an Iterating gives a Cursor, and a Batching gives batches.

Cursors are positions that never change: successor() gives a new cursor, and an old one stays where it was. Iterating is for collections that can be walked again; a consumable stream such as a file or a network body is a Batching, read one batch at a time. map, filter, reduce and find accept both.

The errors below are the role contracts: arrays (whose cursors the language makes) throw them, and other cursors are expected to do the same; the compiler does not check that a user's implementation does.

Public API#

role Cursor#

role Cursor<T>

A position in a walk; successor() moves on by giving a new cursor.

Cursor.available#

available() is bool

Whether there is an item here; false at the end.

Cursor.item#

item() is T

The item here; IterationEnded at the end.

Cursor.successor#

successor() is Cursor<T>

The position after this one; the last item's successor is the end, and the end has none: IterationEnded.

role Iterating#

role Iterating<T>

A collection for can walk, again and again.

Iterating.cursor#

cursor() is Cursor<T>

The position of the first item.

role Batching#

role Batching<T>

A consumable source that hands out its items in batches: for, map, filter and reduce walk each batch as an array and ask for the next one; [] ends the source (#465). Files, sockets and other streams use it instead of a cursor, which would allocate an object per item.

Batching.batch#

batch() is @T

The next batch; [] ends the walk.

object CursorItems#

object CursorItems<T> does Iterating<T>

The items from a cursor on, as an Iterating.

CursorItems.CursorItems#

CursorItems(cursor is Cursor<T>)

Walks from cursor.

CursorItems.cursor#

cursor() is Cursor<T>

The cursor given.
